To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
concept maps are not effective for learning categorized lists.

creating a concept mapping disrupts the processing item-specific information, which results in lower free recall and recognition memory performance than other tasks that require item-specific processing.

concept mapping resulted in a lower recall performance and a lower recognition memory performance, relative to pleasantness rating and sorting, and this effect was observed for both categorized and ad hoc lists.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the processes underlying concept mapping and how they affect the processing of item information.
the processes underlying the creation of a concept map and the effects that concept mapping may have on memory performance.
the processes that underlie concept mapping and the effects of creating concept maps on the processing of information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
concept mapping does not promote the encoding of item-specific information.
concept mapping is an effective tool for learning, however, it is not as effective as sorting and rating for learning the details of a concept.
the creation of concept maps does not enhance learning and may even be detrimental to learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
concept mapping is a task that is not only effective in promoting the processing of relational information, but also effective in disrupting the processing of item specific information.
creating a concept-map is an effective strategy when you are trying to understand and remember a large amount of information, but not necessarily for the information itself.
concept mapping disrupts item-specific encoding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the creation of a concept map is a task that promotes the processing of category information and inhibits item-specific processing.
concept mapping is a task with a strong focus on the relations among items.
concept maps may be a useful tool for learning, but they may also have a negative side effect.
